name: USDA: attaché (GAIN) reports, World Markets and Trade, ERS outlook
access: public: GAIN API and PDFs, FAS PSD circulars, ERS publications
note: GAIN reports are written by USDA's overseas posts and are not official USDA estimates; the official number is the one in the report's own table (USDA Official). Following the desk's rule, the points show how far Post is from USDA and how Post changed its own numbers, not the levels alone.

entries.title: FAS Cotton: World Markets and Trade, November 2026
key_points: Following that sales program, the state reserve bought an estimated 5.5  million bales of imported cotton to replenish stocks, pushing overall cotton imports to 15.0 million  bales in 2023/24, the highest level in a decade.
China cotton consumption is forecast at 42.0 million bales in 2026/27, up less than 1 percent from  2025/26 and below the average level of global growth forecast in 2026/27.
Still, consumption is  forecast to reach the highest level in 15 years.

entries.title: ERS Cotton and Wool Outlook: September 2026 — Special Article: U.S. Hemp Fiber Market Outlook Global Cotton Mill Use Projected To Rise for Fourth Consecutive Year in 2026/27
key_points: Hemp Fiber Market Outlook   Global Cotton Mill Use Projected To Rise for Fourth Consecutive Year in 2026/27 The latest U.S.

Department of Agriculture (USDA) cotton projections for 2026/27 (August–July) indicate that global mill use is forecast to increase 1.8 million bales (1.5 percent) from the previous year to 122.9 million bales, the highest in 6 years (figure 1).
All major spinning countries’ mill use is projected to increase or remain unchanged in 2026/27, led by India and China.

With world cotton stocks expected to decline, global cotton prices are projected to rise moderately in 2026/27 (figure 1).
Global cotton production in 2026/27 is estimated to decline 4.3 million bales (nearly 4 percent) from the previous year to 117.6 million bales.

entries.title: ERS Cotton and Wool Outlook: July 2026 — Global 2026/27 Cotton Mill Use Projected Second Highest in 9 Years
key_points: Economic Research Service | Situation and Outlook Report   CWS-26g | July 14, 2026 Next release is August 14, 2026    Cotton and Wool Outlook: July 2026 Leslie Meyer and Taylor Dew  Global 2026/27 Cotton Mill Use Projected Second Highest in 9 Years The latest U.S.

Department of Agriculture (USDA) cotton projections for 2026/27 (August–July) indicate that world mill use is projected at 122.0 million bales, a 2-percent increase from 2025/26 and the second-highest level since 2017/18 (figure 1).
Cotton mill use for each of the major spinning countries in 2026/27 is unchanged or higher compared with the previous season

All major cotton-producing countries are projected to contribute to the 2026/27 stock reduction.
Global cotton production is forecast at 116.0 million bales, nearly 5.5 percent (6.6 million bales) below 2025/26.

entries.title: ERS Cotton and Wool Outlook: May 2026 — Global 2026/27 Cotton Ending Stocks To Decline as Mill Use Rises Above Production
key_points: Department of Agriculture (USDA) cotton projections for 2026/27 (August–July) indicate a decrease in global ending stocks, compared with 2025/26
World 2026/27 cotton ending stocks are projected at 71.8 million bales, 7 percent (5.4 million bales) lower than the previous year, supporting the potential for higher cotton prices than in 2025/26.
Lower stocks are mainly the result of a 5-percent (6.6 million bales) reduction in the global cotton production forecast (116.0 million bales) from 2025/26.
